text:
olivia: quick follow-up on the batching + access-shim RFC — I sketched a small migration plan to get better throughput for dashboards without blowing up RBAC checks

sam: sharing the plan please

olivia: TL;DR: introduce a thin access-shim that does fast allow/deny for most queries (local cache + token index), wire batching at the executor level for short-lived slices, then gradually flip on global prefetched policies for heavy tenants

jordan: sounds reasonable. main worry is tail latency when the shim miss causes a cold policy fetch

yun: agreed — we should bound that with a 50ms local timeout and async fallback. if the shim times out, executor should run with conservative deny-by-default and surface a telemetry event for sampling

olivia: exact plan I wrote down:

1) implement shim v1: LRU policy cache keyed by (tenant_id, query_scope). return permit/deny synchronously when present
2) executor batching: continuous batching layer groups small panel queries up to 16ms headway or 64 requests, whichever hits first
3) shim misses -> kick off background policy fetch (parallel) and use a conservative short-circuit deny after 50ms; also enqueue request to run using a fallback policy (tenant-global-read-only) if client uses `allow-stale` header
4) telemetry: record shim_hit, shim_miss, fallback_used, fetch_latency, and correlated token/tenant ids for 1% sampled requests

sam: can you paste the rough config we discussed for the batching thresholds?

olivia: sure:```
console.batch_policy = {
  max_batch_latency_ms: 16,
  max_batch_size: 64,
  tenant_priority_window_ms: 5,
  prefetch_on_miss: true
}
console.access_shim = {
  local_ttl_ms: 300000,
  local_cache_size: 20000,
  miss_timeout_ms: 50,
  fallback_policy: "tenant_read_only",
  allow_stale_header: "x-console-allow-stale"
}
```

jordan: thanks. couple of implementation tradeoffs: if we put the shim inline in executor we save a hop but risk making the executor heavier; if shim is sidecar we keep executor lean but add network hop and complexity for batching semantics

yun: my take: start inline with careful CPU budget (shim path is hot but cheap). we can move to sidecar if we hit GC/CPU contention in stress tests

olivia: agreed. rollout plan:
- land shim inline behind feature flag (console.access_shim.v1)
- run internal canary at 5% traffic for 48h, collect shim_miss rate, miss latency, and 95/99th token gen latencies
- increase to 25% if shim miss < 0.5% and p99 latency impact < 3%
- if miss spikes, flip to allow-stale path (no-block fallback) and open incident to debug policy store

sam: do we have expected perf wins? rough numbers?

olivia: on our synthetic dashboard workload: with batching + shim we saw ~2.6x throughput for small panels and ~18% p95 latency improvement overall vs baseline (no shim, no batching). worst-case shim-miss adds ~45-80ms depending on policy-store RTT
jordan: important to flag effect on cost — batching increases GPU/CPU utilization efficiency (lower per-query cost) but longer queues may hurt tail P99 if not bounded
yun: add a safety valve: max_queue_depth_per_executor=256 and an adaptive shedding policy when queue_depth > 80%

olivia: adding that to plan. also want to add an emergency toggle that forces shim to always return deny so we fail-closed in sensitive incidents

infra-bot: deploybot: new feature-flag console.access_shim.v1 created by olivia. use /deploy-canary to start canary

sam: owners? who takes the implementation + telemetry wiring?
olivia: implementation owner: olivia + jordan. telemetry & rollout: yun + sam. infra toggles: infra team (cc infra-bot)

yun: I'll draft the rollout playbook with runbook steps and alert thresholds (shim_miss_rate > 1%, p99 latency up > 5%, fallback_used > 0.5%)

jordan: one more note — update the evals suite to include a 'mixed-tenant' scenario. heavy tenant + many small tenants often changes batching behavior. we should ensure fairness

olivia: good call. I'll update the RFC doc and link to test harness. planning to land a prototype branch tomorrow and open a 48h canary next week

sam: :thumbsup: ping here when canary is live

olivia: will do — thanks everyone
